body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38167

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/794

## What changed

The diffusion scheduler previously returned every execution exception to the triggering request and then continued accepting work. This change treats the two accelerator-fatal signatures reported in the issue as an unrecoverable device state:

- `CUDA driver error: device not ready`
- a `CUDACachingAllocator.cpp` invariant assertion

The triggering request receives an explicit restart-required message, then the scheduler leaves its event loop through the normal reply and cleanup path. Ordinary OOM and unrelated execution errors remain recoverable.

## Reproduction and validation

Failing before, with `scheduler.py` restored from base:

```bash
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-1a8342a614d1/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q /tmp/test_scheduler_device_failure.py
```

This exited 2 because the base implementation lacked the classifier and state transition.

Passing after:

```bash
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-1a8342a614d1/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_scheduler_device_failure.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_warmup_probe_degradation.py
```

Result: 19 passed. The cases cover both reported fatal signatures, the actionable reply and scheduler stop, ordinary OOM, and an unrelated execution error.

One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X was used for an independent float64 sum-of-squares check, which exactly matched the integer closed-form reference. This confirms GPU execution only.

## Limitations

I could not reproduce the original RTX 5070 12 GB / WSL2 / CUDA 13.0 MiniMax-H3 workload: the assigned device is ROCm gfx950-class hardware and the MiniMax-H3 weights plus reporter LoRA were unavailable. Therefore this is reported as `candidate_verified`, not a full-model reproduction. The change intentionally does not relabel `device not ready` as OOM because this environment cannot prove that diagnosis. Automatic restart behavior remains supervisor/deployment-specific.

Full commands, raw output, issue snapshots, and claim metadata are under `reports/j-1a8342a614d1/`.
